# complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

## 1. Node definitions and the complete entropy allowance

For child coefficients x_T,y_T, let Q_T=(x_T^2+y_T^2)/2, e_T=(x_T-y_T)^2/4 and m_T=(|x_T|-|y_T|)^2/4=min(e_T,Q_T-e_T). Put d=sum e_T, mu=sum m_T<=d, L=sum Q_T h2(e_T/Q_T). The exact decrement is Delta H=L+JS(x^2,y^2). The signed logarithmic allocation is J^sgn=sum e_T log2(Q_T/e_T); the required minority allocation is J=sum m_T log2(Q_T/m_T). Each is its own normalized KL expression; they must not be interchanged at a sign-changing endpoint.

Elementary entropy expansion gives J<=L and L<=J^sgn+c d. The first follows because the other half of binary entropy is nonnegative; the second follows from -(1-t)ln(1-t)<=t. Separately L<=J+c mu. The Hellinger inequality JS<=2c mu gives Delta H<=J+3c mu. For completeness: write two probabilities as s(1+t),s(1-t). The nats JS contribution is s[(1+t)ln(1+t)+(1-t)ln(1-t)]/2, at most s(1-sqrt(1-t^2)). The difference starts at zero and has derivative t/sqrt(1-t^2)-artanh(t)>=0, since this derivative's derivative is nonnegative. Summing gives JS_nat<=sum (|x_T|-|y_T|)^2/2=2mu. Thus no unreviewed restriction theorem is needed for this allowance.

## 2. Arbitrary-bias control tree and its retained KL payment

At the unique active node with s remaining controls set u=2^-s and d_s=u a. Its children are 1 and 1+A_(s-1)(g-1). The physical reach probability is w_s=p/u. The empty packet has Q0=1-2d_s+2d_s^2 and signed mismatch e0=d_s^2. In every other packet one child coefficient is zero, so e_T=m_T=Q_T/2, and the total such mismatch is d_s-d_s^2. Hence, for all s including the last one,

    J_s^sgn=d_s-d_s^2+d_s^2 log2(Q0/d_s^2).

If s>=2, the active child's mean 1-2ua is nonnegative; consequently magnitude mismatch agrees with signed mismatch. For s=1 and Eg<0 the empty minority is (1-a/2)^2 rather than a^2/4. We retain the genuine minority cost and only use J_s<=L_s<=J_s^sgn+c d_s. This handles g=-1, g=+1, zero coefficients, and the last-layer sign change. For a=0 the whole tree is constant and all costs are zero.

Since Q0<=1 and 0<d_s<=1,

    J_s^sgn <= d_s+2d_s^2 log2(1/d_s).

Every summand 2^-s(s-log2 a) is nonnegative for a<=2. The infinite sums sum 2^-s=1 and sum s2^-s=2 therefore imply

    sum_s w_s J_s^sgn
      <= p a r + 2p a^2 sum_(s=1)^r 2^-s(s-log2 a)
      <= p a r + 2p a^2(2-log2 a).

Differentiation on 0<a<=2 gives max a(2-log2 a)=4c/e, attained at a=4/e. Combining with J_s<=J_s^sgn+c d_s and sum w_s d_s=rpa proves

    sum_s w_s J_s <= p a[r(1+c)+8c/e] <= K rpa,
    K=1+c+8c/e<7.

Also sum w_s mu_s<=rpa, so the full allowance is at most (K+3c)rpa<12rpa. The remaining expected entropy is exactly pH(g), with expected influence pI(g). Influence is partitioned exactly because each queried control has influence pa and every data influence is p times the core's influence.

These constants require no floating sign calculation. The atanh series gives ln2>2(1/3+1/81)=56/81, and the exponential series gives e>65/24. Thus c<81/56 and c/e< (81/56)(24/65). Substitution proves K<7 and K+3c<12 by rational arithmetic.

## 3. First-revelation ledger and no reuse across descendants

Give this control block one identifier when its first control is queried. Its account holds exactly B_ctrl=rpa, consisting of the distinct physical control-coordinate influences. Its single bill is the complete expected sum of the J_s charges; descendants add subcharges to that bill and cannot open a second account for the same control event. It is closed when the block first becomes known inactive (first mismatch) or known active (r matches). The core account is pI(g), belongs only to the terminal core, and pays pH(g). The two accounts are disjoint; neither is pledged to both a parent and a descendant. This is a first-revelation payment in the sense of the first physical revelation process of a declared event, not an oracle revelation of an unqueried event.

KL credit is generated at the node where its actual (nu_s,Q_s) pair is defined, and consumed once in that node's J_s=mu_s log(1/mu_s)-mu_s D2(nu_s||Q_s). We neither transfer a KL value to another reference law nor claim that the same event earns a fresh credit at every descendant. The paid quantity is the completed block bill, with all these distinct conditional subbills included exactly once. The logarithm is not discarded: the formula in section 2 bounds the post-KL bill explicitly.

On the positive-mean core subfamily (a<=1), mu_s=d_s and the unrebated weighted rarity sum is exactly

    p a [r(r+1)/2+r log2(1/a)].

The weighted KL credit is this expression minus the exact signed J_tree. Thus its quadratic-in-r part is created and consumed within this one control-event account. At a>1 only the last node needs the separate minority endpoint above. This last correction is why simply extending A021's balanced formula by renaming mu would be invalid.

## 4. Direct full-entropy bound for biased activation

Let m=Eg=1-a and use 0log0=0. The empty Fourier coefficient of F is 1-pa; at empty data/nonempty controls it is -pa times the point character; at nonempty data it is p ghat(T) times that character. Summing the actual squared spectrum, with signs retained, gives

    H(F)=pH(g)+2rp a(2-pa)
       +p m^2 log2(m^2)-(p-p^2)a^2 log2(a^2)
       -(1-pa)^2 log2((1-pa)^2).

This is valid for m negative and at all constant endpoints. The m term is nonpositive. The last term is at most 2cpa, by -ln(1-t)<=t/(1-t). For a>=1 the a term is nonpositive; for 0<a<1 its upper bound is 2pa[a log2(1/a)]<=2cpa/e. Therefore

    H(F)<=pH(g)+[4+2c(1+1/e)]rpa < pH(g)+8rpa.

The strict numerical constant follows from c<81/56 and e>65/24: 2c(1+1/e)<7209/1820<4. This improves the conservative mismatch-ledger constant but does not replace the requested J_tree certificate. If H(g)<=C0 I(g), then H(F)<=max(C0,8)I(F); the full sufficient mismatch ledger is <=max(C0,12)I(F). Arbitrary cores still require an actual terminal certificate.

## 5. A complete unbounded family: activated arbitrary bent point-surgery selectors

Let b be any bent function on even k>=4 bits, v any vertex, delta=2^-k, s=b(v), b'=b-2s1_{x=v}, and let t choose b or b' fairly. Define g(x,t) as this selector core, and F=1+A_r(g-1), with arbitrary r>=1. Bent flatness gives I(b)=k/2. Flipping v changes influence in coordinate i by 2delta b(v)b(v^i), since precisely one undirected edge changes status. Consequently

    I(g)=delta+(I(b)+I(b'))/2 >= k/2-(k-1)delta >=7k/16.

Every distribution on the core's 2^(k+1) Fourier labels has H(g)<=k+1<=5k/4. Thus H(g)/I(g)<=20/7<3, a direct terminal certificate. Each child's H is at most k; no threshold or read-once membership is assumed. The exact mean is Eg=Eb-delta s, with |Eb|=sqrt(delta); hence 11/16<=a<=21/16.

The control-first tree therefore has

    J_tree+pH(g) <=7rpa+3pI(g)<=7I(F),
    J_tree+3c sum w_s mu_s+pH(g)<=12I(F),
    H(F)<=8I(F).

The rare point-surgery selector is not queried on inactive paths. On the active leaf its entire entropy, including the surviving kdelta selector logarithm, is paid once by the core account pI(g). That account is not also used for a separate selector bill. In particular r=2k and the quadratic b at v=0 is exactly the accepted B05 sparse-bent obstruction, with its local bad ratio fully absorbed in this complete tree.

## 6. Selector-first complete tree and comparison

Query t at the root, then query controls in each child, stopping on their first mismatch, with terminals b or b'. Let a_*=(1-Eb+1-Eb')/2=a and Ibar=(I(b)+I(b'))/2. Root disagreement is d=pdelta. Because the root children differ at exactly one point of the (r+k)-cube, every Fourier ratio is an even integer: an integer Walsh sum of 2^(r+k) signs is even. Thus the signed mismatch e=d^2 is the minority in every packet, mu=d. Its exact bill is sum_T e log(Q/e), and its KL representation implies

    J_root<=d log2(1/d)=pdelta(r+k).

The two child control-tree bills average to at most 7rpa. Their expected terminal entropy is p[H(b)+H(b')]/2<=pk. Since a>=11/16>=delta, the r part of J_root is <=rpa. Since Ibar>=k/2-kdelta>=7k/16, its k part is <=(16delta/7)pIbar, and terminal entropy is <=(16/7)pIbar. Therefore, for k>=4,

    J_selector-first+terminal <=8rpa+(17/7)pIbar<=8I(F),
    I(F)=rpa+pIbar+pdelta.

The full 3c mu allowance is <=3c(rpa+pdelta), so full sufficient ledger<=13I(F). Influence accounts here are distinct: root selector pdelta; queried controls rpa; terminal data pIbar. The selector bill uses additional control/data allowances once; the stated constants include these extra debits. No assertion that selector-first is optimal is made. Both actual complete trees are linearly paid although the isolated selector is not paid by its own influence with a universal constant.

For the original positive quadratic b at zero, Ibar=k/2+kdelta, Eg=sqrt(delta)-delta, and I(g)=k/2+(k+1)delta. These identities are checked exactly. Terminal-entropy placement differs: control-first leaves the full selector core; selector-first retains the root selector bill and leaves its two children. The entropy difference is exactly the core's own restriction decrement, multiplied by p, so neither tree silently omits it.

## 7. Multiple events and descendants: disjoint product extension

For any finite number M of independent components of section 5, let f=product_(j=1)^M F_j. Process components in fixed order, querying a component's controls until it fails or activates, leaving its certified core unqueried; continue until every component is resolved. The tree has depth at most sum r_j. Its leaves are products of the active cores and constant signs. A core is activated with probability p_j. Entropy and influence of disjoint products add by tensor Fourier factorization.

At a node querying component j, child Fourier coefficients are x_T b_R,y_T b_R. Their Q and m are multiplied by b_R^2; the ratio Q/m is unchanged, and sum_R b_R^2=1. Thus J, mu and queried influence are precisely the component's quantities, even with earlier terminal cores and later unresolved components present. Averaging over earlier histories restores the original reach weights for component j. Hence total J and expected terminal entropy are the sums of the component bills, and all bounds in sections 5-6 add. The simultaneous rarity events never share an account or a physical coordinate. This proves the stated unbounded-dimensional, unbounded-component family, rather than merely finitely checking a quadratic example.

First unsupported universal line: every arbitrary Boolean f admits such a controlled-event decomposition, or another physical stopping rule with the same complete linear bill and uniformly certified terminal cores. Neither is proved. Allowing arbitrary g in section 2 without its terminal certificate leaves pH(g) unpaid; the threshold paper's Corollary 8.10 explains why this cannot be treated as a negligible remainder.

Hence b(q)=-2(1-q)^2log2(1-q)=2cq-3cq^2+R(q), with R(q)=+4c sum_(j>=3) q^j/[j(j-1)(j-2)]. Its decrement remainder R(u)-R(2u)/2 is negative. The old A023 review's multiplication and its acceptance of A021-UNIFORM-RARE-CORE-EXPANSION@1 were wrong. Retract that acceptance; narrow its report-wide endorsement. The separate exact A021-CONTROL-FIRST-KL-LEDGER@1 remains valid.

This confirms the objection without relying on a floating decimal. The first A023 family/tree claim used its direct node formula, elementary entropy inequalities and exact influence counting; neither R nor the decrement remainder occurred. Its constants and family theorem survive unchanged. No new contribution to A021 v2 is asserted, and no copied accepted v1 status may continue to authorize its false tail sign.

## 2. Exact resources for the overlapping events

At a common control coordinate, pivotality needs all other common controls active, the union of exclusives active, and g=-1. Its influence is u a beta. Each first-exclusive coordinate has influence u a p(1-q); each second-exclusive coordinate has influence u a q(1-p). Data influences are u beta times the core influences. Summing yields the stated partition. Terminal core probability is u beta, not u(p+q); paths where both events hold still have one copy of g and one terminal bill.

The rule is determined only by previously queried physical values. A mismatch of a common control stops immediately. A successful first exclusive event resolves the union and stops at g. If it fails, query the second exclusive event, stopping at its first mismatch or its success. A fixed-order tree that queries skipped irrelevant controls has the same ledger, since those splits have B=d=I(child product)=0; this equivalence is used by the finite implementation.

## 3. A local exposure inequality, not a guessed transfer

Consider a first-exclusive node with l controls remaining. Write C for the second event, whose conditional probability remains q, and rho=2^-(l-1). Its children are

    f0=1+C(g-1),
    f1=1+[C+(1-C)A_(l-1)](g-1).

Disagreement is d=a rho(1-q)/2. In Fourier fibers involving a NONEMPTY subset of the remaining l-1 first-exclusive controls, f0 has zero coefficient. Therefore each such parent packet has equal spectral-bit masses and B=2e. The squared point indicator's fraction on its empty label is rho, so these fibers have total mismatch (1-rho)d and erasure 2(1-rho)d exactly. All other fibers have total mismatch rho d and total packet mass M<=1. Concavity gives their erasure <=M h2(rho d/M)<=h2(rho d), since the latter expression increases with M. This is valid for signed mismatch as well as magnitude minority: binary entropy is the same whichever half is smaller. No unsigned substitution is made in a KL formula.

Using h2(x)<=x log2(e/x), obtain

    B/d<=2(1-rho)+rho log2(e/(rho d)).

The more general sufficient criterion is a(1-q)>e/8. Under this criterion rho d>e rho^2/16 and

    B/d<2+2rho[1+log2(1/rho)]<=4.

The final inequality is dyadic, not a continuous maximization: rho=2^-j and (j+1)2^-j<=1 for every integer j>=0, with equality only j=0,1. In our two-event class q<=1/2 and a>=11/16, so a(1-q)>=11/32>e/8. This proves first-exclusive goodness in all widths, independent of core dimension or Fourier details.

For a common-control node the inactive child is constant and the active child is an activation of the union-core function. After the first-exclusive event fails, a second-exclusive node is likewise constant-child. For any such split define d=Pr(child=-1). Its signed packet formula is

    Jsgn=d-d^2+d^2 log2((1-2d+2d^2)/d^2),
    B<=Jsgn+c d <=[1+c+2c/e]d<4d,

where d log2(1/d)<=c/e. At d=0 the split contributes zero. This formula remains valid for a negative child mean; minority allocation and signed allocation are not equated. Thus every node before the certified core is reached is good.

Rational constants: ln2>2(1/3+1/81)=56/81, hence c<81/56. Also 65/24<e<65/24+1/100<11/4: the exponential tail from 1/5! is bounded by the geometric ratio 1/6. These bounds prove 1+c+2c/e<4, 4+2c<7 and 4+3c<9 by Fraction arithmetic. The detailed exposure proof is saved immediately in OVERLAP_GOOD_NODE_PROOF.md.

## 4. Complete cost, terminal entropy and face ownership

For an actual split, Delta H=B+JS and JS<=2c d. One elementary proof writes two probabilities as s(1+z),s(1-z) and uses [(1+z)ln(1+z)+(1-z)ln(1-z)]/2<=1-sqrt(1-z^2). The derivative of the difference is z/sqrt(1-z^2)-artanh(z)>=0 on [0,1]. Summing gives JS<=2c mu<=2c d, with mu the magnitude minority mass. Thus the exact entropy telescope gives H(F)<=4I_ctrl+2cI_ctrl+H_leaf. Likewise Jminor<=B and mu<=d give the two required retained-KL bounds without discarding a terminal remainder.

Let Q(f)=2^(1-n) times its number of odd 2-faces, meaning corner product -1. At a split, faces not using that direction partition into child cubes, and faces using it are precisely boundary edges of the child product. Hence Q(f)=I(g_v h_v)/2+[Q(g_v)+Q(h_v)]/2. This proves first-revelation face ownership: every face is charged exactly at the first split along one of its two directions. The stopping tree retains expected Q(leaf), just as it retains expected H(leaf). We do NOT spend every odd face: since all its control nodes are good, the localized bad-node part is exactly zero. Total unlocalized face cost may still be large.

Coordinate ownership is also explicit. There is one common block account s u a beta, not two copies attributed to the two events. The exclusive block accounts include their survival factors (1-q) and (1-p). One terminal core account u beta I(g) pays u beta H(g). Each physical coordinate is queried at most once on any history; every expected debit is included once in I_ctrl. This resolves shared-control/shared-core ownership for this declared two-event family.

## 5. Unconditional all-dimensional terminal family

Let b be any bent sign on even k>=4 bits and v any vertex. Let b' flip b only at v, and let g choose b or b' by one fresh fair selector. Put delta=2^-k and s_v=b(v). Bent flatness gives I(b)=k/2 and |Eb|=sqrt(delta). An edge-count change gives I_i(b')-I_i(b)=2delta b(v)b(v^i), and selector influence delta. Hence

    I(g)>=k/2-(k-1)delta>=7k/16,
    H(g)<=k+1<=5k/4,
    H(g)/I(g)<=20/7<3.

The exact mean is Eg=Eb-delta s_v, so a>=1-sqrt(delta)-delta>=11/16. Thus every such core meets the exposure hypothesis, with independently unbounded k,s,r,t. Combining its certified terminal cost with section 4 yields H(F)<7I(F), J_tree+terminal<=4I(F), full sufficient mismatch ledger<9I(F). This improves the earlier disjoint-event constants while paying the overlapping point masks. The elementary core H/I bound itself is not claimed as novel.

## 6. Exact finite comparison of four COMPLETE orders

The frozen grid has s=0,1,2; r,t=1,2; k=2,4, with the positive quadratic bent core flipped at zero. That is 24 actual roots, each with four complete orders, plus its control-first stopping tree. Original coordinate order is common/exclusive-A/exclusive-B/data/selector. Orders are explicitly:

All 24 stopping trees have Q_bad=0, as the all-width proof predicts. The terminal entropy in the stopping theorem is not silently erased. k=2 is only a finite endpoint test, not part of the k>=4 terminal theorem. # exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

A023/B05 stage 3, run 20261013T223305Z-fleet05-A023-amortized-rarity-budget. Uniform physical Boolean signs, all entropy/KL in bits. Let U,V,W be compatible point indicators on disjoint control blocks of independently arbitrary widths R,T,L>=1, X one fair physical separator bit, and g an independent BALANCED Boolean core. The controller has three overlapping events:

    A=XU OR XV OR WUV, F=1+A(g-1).

Write p=2^-L, q=2^-R, r=2^-T, beta=q+r-qr, eta=pqr, pi=(beta+eta)/2 and e=beta-eta. The physical stopping policy queries X first, resolves WUV if X=0 or U OR V if X=1, and stops at a constant or at g. It retains terminal entropy pi H(g). Core entropy is not discarded even on very rare paths.

All-dimensional scoped result: every descendant control node is strictly K=4-good; the separator may be bad and is not assumed good. Its exact one-use odd-face price is c_X=Jrem+e I(g)/2, where J(B)=I(1-2B)/2 and

    d_X=e/2,
    Jrem=[(L+R+T)eta+R q(1-r)+T r(1-q)]/2,
    I_ctrl=J(A)=d_X+Jrem, I_terminal=pi I(g).

The stopping tree has Q_bad either zero or c_X, hence Q_bad<=I(F)-d_X. With H(g)<=C0 I(g), a marked separator reserve spent once proves H(F)<=max(5+2/ln2,C0+1)I(F). Without this terminal hypothesis, the exact upper ledger is

    H(F)<=(5+2/ln2)J(A)+pi H(g)+(e/2)I(g).

The complete genuine minority/KL bill plus terminal is <=5J(A)+pi H(g)+(e/2)I(g); with its separate 3mu/ln2 allowance it is <=(5+3/ln2)J(A)+pi H(g)+(e/2)I(g).

For g=z times the selector between any even-k>=4 bent sign and its flip at one vertex, g is balanced and H(g)/I(g)<3. This gives H(F)<8I(F), retained J+terminal<=5I(F), and full sufficient mismatch ledger<10I(F) uniformly in L,R,T,k. No repeated-child bank or universal FEI theorem is claimed. The new theorem extends the existing A023 overlap claim; it does not open a separate broad candidate.

# complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

## 1. Independent witness review before extending the mechanism

A021's actual controller is A=x1x2 OR x1x3 OR x0x2x3. Direct positive-literal truth tables, integer Walsh transforms and independent edge counts give pi=7/16, J(A)=3/4, d_x0=1/16 and face price I(F0F1)/2=1/4 for g=z. Its B-4d is exactly the source's rational prime-log expression, independently certified positive. The original fixed x0-first control order has Q_bad=1/4; x1-first has zero on this fixture.

For any balanced g, the nonempty-core Fourier rows have controller coefficients multiplied by ghat(T); their erasure kernel is homogeneous of degree two. Summing ghat(T)^2 gives one, while the pure-control row is unchanged. Thus control-node B and d are precisely the dictator-core quantities. The face price depends on I(g), not only balance. REVIEW_A021_WITNESS.md records HOLDS for exactly this source-bound scope, without accepting A021's tensor-prefix or finite exhaustive conclusions. No source repair was supplied.

## 2. The three-event extension and actual coordinate partition

The separator controller children are A0=WUV and A1=U OR V, with A0 contained in A1. Their densities are eta and beta. The parent density is pi, not beta+eta. Every active history reaches the same g once, including histories where multiple event descriptions hold.

A point indicator of width m and density rho has J=m rho by directed-edge counting. Therefore J(A0)=(L+R+T)eta and J(A1)=R q(1-r)+T r(1-q). The separator influence is (beta-eta)/2=e/2 because a balanced g is negative on half the data cube. Each other physical controller coordinate has its half-averaged child influence. Hence

    I(F)=J(A)+pi I(g), J(A)=e/2+[J(A0)+J(A1)]/2.

The W-coordinate contribution to Jrem is L eta/2; the U block's is R[q(1-r)+eta]/2, and the V block's is T[r(1-q)+eta]/2. These are actual physical coordinate accounts, not independently credited boundaries of the three named events. The formulas are verified against direct edges in every frozen case.

## 3. Descendants are good; the separator is treated separately

In the X=0 child, the controller is one point conjunction WUV. Every queried control has a constant inactive child. For signed disagreement d, exact Fourier grouping gives Jsgn=d-d^2+d^2log2((1-2d+2d^2)/d^2), and B<=Jsgn+c d, c=1/ln2. Thus B/d<=1+c+2c/euler<4. Here euler denotes the exponential constant, distinct from the controller density e. Endpoints d=0 contribute zero. This is an actual binary erasure statement and does not equate magnitude mismatch to signed disagreement.

In the X=1 child, U OR V is the previous two-event fresh-block case with a=1. At a U-control node with remaining point probability rho=2^-j, mismatch is d=rho(1-r)/2. Fibers with nonempty remaining-U label have one zero child amplitude and contribute 2(1-rho)d exactly. Other fibers have mismatch rho d, total packet mass at most one, and contribution <=h2(rho d). Hence B/d<=2(1-rho)+rho log2(euler/(rho d)). Since (1-r)>=1/2>euler/8, this is strictly <2+2rho(1+j)<=4. After U fails the V nodes are again constant-child; after U succeeds stop immediately at g. No descendant bad-control face bill exists in either branch, in any widths.

The X separator itself is never priced by an assumed fresh-event lemma. The finite checks happen to find it good in the frozen domain; the theorem and reserve work even if it is bad outside that domain. Root-goodness in all widths is a separate unsupported strengthening.

## 4. Exact root face price and the first-revelation reserve

Let D=A1-A0. It is an indicator of density e, and F0F1=1+D(g-1). Balance gives I(F0F1)=e I(g)+J(D). Direct control edges yield

    J(D)=R q(1-r)+T r(1-q)+(L+R+T)eta=2Jrem.

For example, a U pivot changes D if V=0, or if V=1 and W=1; its probability contribution is q[(1-r)+p r]. The analogous V contribution and the W contribution prove the displayed identity. Equivalently, the cut edges of A0 and A1 are disjoint, so their symmetric-difference boundary adds exactly. Therefore c_X=Jrem+e I(g)/2. Since e/2<=pi, c_X<=Jrem+pi I(g)=I(F)-d_X. Since descendants are good, Q_bad is zero if the root is good and c_X if it is bad.

This is a one-use face account. Odd faces involving X are charged only when X is first revealed, since Q(f)=I(f0f1)/2+[Q(f0)+Q(f1)]/2. The identity follows by partitioning cube faces into those lying inside children and those projecting to cut edges of their product. Descendants cannot debit these same faces.

Influence reserves must also be marked before descent. At rate K=5+2c, give each nonseparator physical control coordinate K times its expected influence. Reserve one unit of that rate exclusively for c_X's controller part; descendants get only K-1=4+2c. Their full erasure/recombination cost is within that remaining rate. Each terminal-core coordinate at rate C0+1 reserves one unit for the root's data face part; terminal entropy receives only C0. The actual data fraction consumed is e/(2pi)<=1; the leftover from this reserved unit is eta I(g), nonnegative. The separator's own influence is priced at K. Root charges are paid once from these named capacities. No reserve is recreated at child nodes. It would be invalid to apply the same one-unit reservation at every ancestor of an arbitrarily deep separator tree.

## 5. Entropy/KL telescope with all terminal cost included

For any actual split, Delta H=B+JS and JS<=2c mu<=2c d, with magnitude minority mu. This follows from the scalar inequality [(1+t)ln(1+t)+(1-t)ln(1-t)]/2<=1-sqrt(1-t^2): its difference has derivative t/sqrt(1-t^2)-artanh(t)>=0. Summing across packets gives the JS claim.

At the separator B_X<=4d_X+c_X irrespective of badness. For a good node this is immediate. Otherwise B<=h2(d)<=d log2(1/d)+c d<=c_X+4d, because the cube edge-isoperimetric inequality gives d log2(1/d)<=I(F0F1)/2. An elementary proof of that inequality is as follows: a set of m vertices spans at most m log2(m)/2 edges. Induct across a cube coordinate with child sizes a<=b; the new internal edges are at most a, and (a+b)log2(a+b)-a log2(a)-b log2(b)>=2a follows from h2(a/(a+b))>=2a/(a+b). The boundary therefore has at least m log2(2^n/m) edges, yielding the normalized influence assertion.

Summing the actual fair stopping tree gives

    H(F)<=(4+2c)J(A)+Q_bad+pi H(g)
         <=(4+2c)d_X+(5+2c)Jrem+pi H(g)+(e/2)I(g).

This is stronger than the stated uniform-rate upper ledger and displays which root-coordinate capacity is unspent. The entire pi H(g) is retained. If H(g)<=C0 I(g), the marked account proves H(F)<=max(5+2c,C0+1)I(F).

For the requested retained KL bill, define m_T=(|a_T|-|b_T|)^2/4, mu=sum m_T, Q_T=(a_T^2+b_T^2)/2, nu=m/mu, and Jminor=sum m_T log2(Q_T/m_T)=mu[log2(1/mu)-D2(nu||Q)]. Always Jminor<=B and mu<=d. Therefore J_tree+pi H(g)<=4J(A)+Q_bad+pi H(g)<=5J(A)+pi H(g)+(e/2)I(g). Its additive 3c sum mu allowance is at most 3c J(A), giving the full source ledger. No raw mu log term is substituted for Jminor, no KL reference is transferred across nodes, and terminal entropy is not omitted.

## 6. A nontrivial unbounded terminal family

Let b be any bent sign on even k>=4 bits, let b' flip b at one vertex v, and let h fairly select b or b'. Balance it by an independent sign z, so g=z h. Flatness gives I(b)=k/2. A one-point flip changes each data influence by 2delta b(v)b(v^i), delta=2^-k, and h's selector influence is delta. Thus I(g)=1+I(h)>=1+k/2-(k-1)delta, while H(g)=H(h)<=k+1. For k>=4 this ratio is <3. Its terminal certificate uses only a proved support/edge bound, not an unproved arbitrary-core estimate.

With c<81/56, 5+2c<8 and 5+3c<10 by exact rational arithmetic. Hence the full family has H(F)<8I(F), J+terminal<=5I(F), and full sufficient mismatch ledger<10I(F). L,R,T and k remain independent and unbounded. For fixed core and L, R=T going to infinity makes event density and total influence vanish; the same constants still apply. This is a three-event overlap extension of the existing first-revelation mechanism, not a claimed novel bound for bent cores themselves.

First unsupported universal line: the sum of marked separator reservations remains bounded per actual physical coordinate in arbitrary overlapping/deep controllers, with all terminals certified. The present one-separator reserve is not an arbitrary-depth potential. A021's balanced selector exposure shows precisely why repeating a residual J bank without consumption is invalid. No automatic maximal-influence policy, universal zero-badness statement, or full FEI follows here.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

The full proof is in BIAS_TRANSPORT.tex; BOUNDARY_CREDITS.md gives analytic endpoint expansions and their uniformity limits. Let Eplus denote the corrected entropy, D=I-Var, e(u)=u log2(1/u), m_i=E f_i, v_i=1-m_i^2, and mu the actual product law of child outputs. The composing definition is

    Eplus_mu(g)=sum_{S nonempty} P_mu(S) log2(product_{i in S} v_i/P_mu(S)).

There is no output-variance numerator. For physical uniform f, H(f)=Eplus(f)+e((E f)^2). Conditional nonempty entropy differs by the exact v log2(1/v) normalization term.

Set a_i=E_{mu_-i}(D_i g)^2, a bounded pivotal probability. For v_i>0 it equals Inf_i^mu(g)/v_i; at v_i=0 use contraction, and the polynomial a_i only as an extension for zero-weight inner contributions. The known unique-disjoint-union Fourier identity gives

    Eplus(F)=Eplus_mu(g)+sum_i a_i Eplus(f_i),
    I(F)=sum_i a_i I(f_i),
    D(F)=D_mu(g)+sum_i a_i D(f_i).                         (1)

After querying x inside j let delta Z=Z-(Z+ + Z-)/2, beta=(m_j+ - m_j-)/2, d=Inf_x(f_j), t=a_j, b=E D_j g, M=E F. The remaining physical inputs stay uniform. Only the output law changes. For i!=j, a_i is affine in m_j, hence its child average equals its original value; t is independent of m_j. Consequently

    delta Eplus(F)=delta Eplus_mu(g)+t delta Eplus(f_j),
    delta I(F)=t d,
    delta D_mu(g)=beta^2(t-b^2),
    delta D(F)=t d-b^2 beta^2.                            (2)

The variance calculation uses delta Var(f_j)=beta^2 and delta Var(F)=b^2 beta^2. Define

    T=delta Eplus_mu(g)+delta e(M^2)-t delta e(m_j^2).

Then the exact full-FEI surplus transfer is

    delta H(F)=t delta H(f_j)+T,
    delta(C I-H)(F)=t delta(C I-H)(f_j)-T.                (3)

The C(D)-Eplus slack has its own cocycle; the empty-atom reserve C Var-e(mean^2) converts it to full-FEI slack. C beta^2(t-b^2) is not free additional influence: it cancels in that conversion.

For the directly physical representation F=A(z)+B(z)f_j(u), Booleanity gives AB=0 and A^2+B^2=1 pointwise, with t=E B^2. Define L(a,c)=e(a^2)+e(c^2)-e(a^2+c^2). The exact erasure transfer is

    B_x(F)=t B_x(f_j)+R,
    R=sum_Z L(Ahat_Z+m_j Bhat_Z,beta Bhat_Z)-t L(m_j,beta). (4)

Each nonempty residual inner set contributes by homogeneity exactly t times its inner erasure cost. Only the inner empty residual set changes: its amplitude becomes Ahat+m_j Bhat. Removing its old contribution proves the negative subtraction in (4). This fills A057's stated descendant gap for arbitrary means and deterministic endpoints. With the actual physical JS terms,

    T=R+JS_x(F)-t JS_x(f_j).                              (5)

For t>0, beta!=0, scalar binary entropy and log-sum also give

    R <= t beta^2 log2([1-t+(m_j^2+beta^2)t]/[t beta^2])
         +t beta^2 log2(e)-t L(m_j,beta).                 (6)

Here sum_Z(Ahat+m_j Bhat)^2=1-t+m_j^2 t. The displayed bound leaves outer rarity t visible; it does not assert R<=K t d.

Retain the existing mismatch rebate using actual inner children: q_U=(fhat_j+(U)^2+fhat_j-(U)^2)/2, r_U=(|fhat_j+(U)|-|fhat_j-(U)|)^2/4, eta=sum r_U, nu=r/eta. For eta>0,

    delta H(F) <= t eta[log2(1/eta)-KL_2(nu||q)+3/ln2]+T. (7)

At eta=0 the inner decrement vanishes exactly; T need not vanish. Dropping KL or replacing the actual composed children by inner children would be invalid.

At beta=0, all output laws are unchanged and T=R=0: the entire decrement transports by t. For a signed dictator outer gate T=0 at every endpoint. Contract deterministic outputs before forming a normalized basis or dividing by a deficit. Corrected entropy cancels the outer v_j log(1/v_j) term exactly. For a fixed finite gate and fixed other biases, its corrected endpoint drift is O(v_j), with possible second-order v_j^2 log(1/v_j) terms from newly zero normalized coefficients; this is not an arity-uniform remainder.

The log(1/mean) requested by the lead appears in the scalar subtraction. At fixed nonzero m and beta->0, if Z(m)=sum_{Ahat+m Bhat=0} Bhat^2 then R=-Z(m) beta^2 log(1/beta^2)+O(beta^2); its leading rare-beta logarithm is nonpositive. At m=0, R=kappa beta^2 log(1/beta^2)+O(beta^2), kappa=sum_{Ahat!=0} Bhat^2<=t. In the iterated regime beta=o(|m|), m->0, the beta^2 coefficient has kappa log(1/m^2)+O(1). The exact subtraction resolves this nonuniform crossover. This logarithmic component is bounded by [2/(e ln2)]t d, since |beta|<=d and u log(1/u)<=1/e. It is A057's affordable bank, not the whole erasure payment or a claim that all nodes are good. Bad-node status requires the full comparison B_x(F)>K t d.

A near-dictator calibration demonstrates the missing credit: f_j=x(1-2 1_{z=0}) with r control bits and a two-input AND outer with another fair literal. At query x, eta_inner=0 and delta H(f_j)=0; t=1/2 and delta I(F)=1/2, but delta H(F)=T tends to 2 bits (R tends to 1 and JS_F to 1). Explicit point-defect spectral masses give the vanishing entropy remainder O(r 2^-r). This is a constant-price calibration, not an unbounded bad-node family.

# A025: strict threshold 2 fails localized odd-face payment

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

Q_bad,K(T) := sum_{v: B_{i_v}(f_v)>K d_v} pi_v I(g_v h_v)/2 <= Kprime I(f),

where g_v,h_v are the actual fair Boolean children, d_v=Inf_{i_v}(f_v), B_i=H(S_i|S_-i), and pi_v is the physical probability of reaching v. All entropies are in bits. This stage proves failure for K=2 (and K<2), even for every complete adaptive tree of its explicit family. It does not refute the existence of a sufficiently large K,Kprime. We use {0,1} coordinates as a relabeling of the uniform sign cube. The selected family has output rarity 2^-n and dimension n.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

Let f_n(x)=1-2*1_{x=0}. This is a genuine Boolean sign, equal to -1 at one vertex only. Put q=2^-n. Its Fourier coefficients are a_empty=1-2q and a_S=-2q for every nonempty S. Each coordinate has influence d=2q, so I(f_n)=2nq.

At any split of a live m-variable point-defect node, one child is constant +1 and one is f_{m-1}, up to translation. Hence their product is f_{m-1}, and

c_m := I(g h)/2 = (m-1)2^(1-m).

The spectra show that each nonempty residual Fourier pair has equal masses 4q_m^2, where q_m=2^-m. There are 2^(m-1)-1 such pairs. Only the empty residual pair is exceptional, with masses A=(1-2q_m)^2 and D=4q_m^2. Consequently

B_i(f_m)=4q_m-8q_m^2+E(A,D),
E(A,D)=A log2(1+D/A)+D log2(1+A/D).

For m>=3, A/D=(2^(m-1)-1)^2>=9. Thus

E(A,D)>D log2(A/D)>=4q_m^2 log2(9)>8q_m^2,

so B_i(f_m)>4q_m=2d for every coordinate. At m=2 the spectrum is uniform on four sets and B_i=1=2d exactly; at m=1 the function is a character and B_i=0. Therefore the strict K=2 bad nodes are exactly the live m>=3 nodes.

Any adaptive complete physical tree has exactly one live path; every restriction along it remains a translated point defect. The probability of reaching its m-variable live node is 2^-(n-m), irrespective of coordinate order. All other reached nodes are constant and have zero charge. Thus, for every such tree and every n>=3,

Q_bad,2(T)=sum_{m=3}^n 2^-(n-m)c_m
          =2^(1-n)[n(n-1)/2-1],
Q_bad,2(T)/I(f_n)=(n-1)/2-1/n -> infinity.

For any fixed Kprime>=0, every integer n>=ceil(2Kprime+3) yields a strict violation. If K<2, the m=2 node is also bad, and Q_bad,K/I=(n-1)/2. This is a counterfamily to a threshold choice and its claimed linear global charge, not merely a finite failed coefficient.

To check the face normalization independently, define Q(f)=2^(1-n) times the number of 2-faces with corner product -1. Faces not involving the split coordinate partition into the two child cubes and contribute their average Q. A face involving that coordinate is odd exactly when its residual edge has different values of gh. The number of such edges is 2^(n-2) I(gh), so their normalized contribution is I(gh)/2. This proves Q(f)=I(gh)/2+(Q(g)+Q(h))/2. For f_n, precisely the binomial(n,2) faces containing its exceptional vertex are odd. The total Q/I=(n-1)/2 agrees with the localized formula after subtracting the single m=2 payment 1/n.

The threshold boundary is essential. Since E(A,D)<=D log2(e(A+D)/D) and A+D<=1 for m>=2,

B_i(f_m)/d <= 2+2^-m(4m-8+2log2(e)) < 2+4m2^-m.

Here the entropy estimate follows from -(1-t)ln(1-t)<=t with t=D/(A+D). For fixed K>2, let M_K be the largest integer m>=2 satisfying 4m2^-m>K-2, or take M_K=1 if that set is empty. It is finite. Only nodes with m<=M_K can be bad. Thus every complete tree of this family satisfies

Q_bad,K(T)/I(f_n) <= M_K(M_K-1)/(2n) -> 0.

This family supplies no large-K obstruction. It also satisfies H(f_n)/I(f_n)<4 for n>=2: its tail entropy is (2^n-1)4q^2(2n-2), while the empty atom entropy is <=(4q-4q^2)log2(e). After division by 2nq the sum is <4-4/n+2log2(e)/n<4. Its Shannon ratio tends to 4, consistent with the campaign's point-defect controls.

No line in the stated threshold-2 theorem remains unsupported. The first unpaid line for the intended universal route is: there exist sufficiently large fixed K,Kprime such that the localized payment holds on arbitrary Boolean functions for an appropriately quantified physical tree, with terminal entropy retained. This stage neither proves nor disproves that line. A stopping tree may terminate before all coordinates are read; the theorem does not claim that every stopping strategy fails.

For integer Walsh coefficients a_S and N=2^n, set A=a_T^2 and D=a_{T+i}^2. Multiplying (A+D)^(A+D)/(A^A D^D) over pairs and comparing with 2^(K sum D) exactly certifies the strict logarithmic sign. Zero entries contribute a factor one. The physical cost at a node is the directed edge-count of gh divided by N. In the DP, its integer numerator adds to both child numerators because their fair 1/2 weights cancel the halved child cube size. Therefore the DP returns exact rational cost/influence ratios.

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

This construction is one concrete nested rare-flip family, not all possible rare towers.

The activated moments are exactly

    p_j=a_j c_j,
    i_j=a_j[J_j+2r_j c_j],
    q_j=a_j[R_j+r_j J_j+r_j(r_j-1)c_j].

Each unordered face pair is counted once. Data-data faces through the flipped point, data-selector, data-previous, selector-previous and previous-previous faces give R_j. Control-core and control-control pairs give the two remaining activated terms. Thus the proof keeps the cross-level faces that a naive sum of isolated root charges would miss.

For all integer r, r2^-r<=1/2 and r(r-1)2^-r<=3/4; for even k>=2, delta<=1/4, kdelta<=1/2 and k^2delta<=1. Induction gives i_j<=k+2 and q_j<=k+4 uniformly in depth and all r_j. Consequently R_L<=k/4+5/2. The lower bound i_L>=a_L k/2 is preserved.

A split with one constant child has exactly B=2d(1-d)+Psi(d^2,(1-d)^2). Its entropy bound gives B/d<=2+log2(e)/sqrt(e)<3. The outermost controls therefore incur no K=4 bad cost. They leave one active core branch of physical probability a_L. The entire remaining bad-face cost, whatever subsequent complete order is used, is at most a_L R_L by the face telescope. Therefore

    Q_bad,4(T)/I(F_L) <= a_L R_L/(a_L k/2)
                         <=1/2+5/k<=3.

This is one owned post-outer-control face reserve. It does not spend i_L anew at each nested level. For k>=4 the displayed bound is <=7/4. Terminal entropy is zero because the computed/theorem trees are complete with constant leaves. An early stop at the exposed core would retain H(core); it is not paid by declaring the controls finished.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

not substitute h2(d) for the actual spectral erasure entropy.

Write alpha=2^-s, eta=2^-(L+R+T), e=2^-R+2^-T-2^-(R+T)-eta,

For completeness, the JS bank used to telescope entropy follows from
the scalar inequality

    [p ln(2p/(p+q))+q ln(2q/(p+q))]/2
      <= (sqrt(p)-sqrt(q))^2/2.

Put x=(p-q)/(p+q). Its proof reduces to
[(1+x)ln(1+x)+(1-x)ln(1-x)]/2<=1-sqrt(1-x^2);

    H(F)<=(4+2/ln2)(I_separator+I_other)+pi H(g).

# A028 stopping-tree payment

Full FEI remains OPEN. This run proves a finite unbalanced-activation stopping ledger and independently reconstructs four existing B06 claims at their stated scopes. The new claim awaits independent review; registry adoption and supervisor copying are not asserted.

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

All physical inputs are independent uniform signs; Fourier coefficients use the normalized Walsh basis; entropy and KL are in bits. Let g be ANY finite-dimensional Boolean sign, delta=Pr(g=-1), r>=1, p=2^-r, and A_r the indicator of one assignment of r fresh physical controls. Put F=1+A_r(g-1). The control-first tree queries controls in a fixed order, stops at the first failure, and otherwise reaches g with probability p.

At a split let a,b be the actual child Fourier coefficients, q_T=(a_T^2+b_T^2)/2, m_T=(|a_T|-|b_T|)^2/4, mu=sum m_T, and nu=m/mu when mu>0. Define the complete nonnegative logarithmic bill J=sum m_T log2(q_T/m_T)=mu[log2(1/mu)-D_2(nu||q)], with zero terms omitted. Write c=log2(e). The recovered split upper bound is Delta H<=J+3c mu. We prove

    E sum J <= (3+c/e) Q,
    E sum (J+3c mu) <= kappa Q,
    Q=2rp delta,  kappa=3+c(3+1/e)<8.

Therefore if g has an FEI-certified terminal allowance K I(g), the FULL expected upper path bill plus terminal allowance is at most max(kappa,K) I(F). This is uniform in dimension, r, delta and the spectrum of g. It pays the mismatch/KL bill itself, not merely the smaller exact entropy decrement.

The same constant holds for every finite expression built from certified terminals by fresh point activations, sign negations, and products on disjoint physical supports, with arbitrary expression depth and control arities. Fix k0,M0 for bounded-overlap terminals; their constants must not be treated as uniform when these parameters grow. Terminal products are certified by exact disjoint additivity; for an activation-only expression the reached leaves are the original recovered terminal or constants.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### 1. Actual control-node packets, including the sign-changing last child

At the active node with s controls left, let u=2^-s. The children are constant +1 and 1+A_(s-1)(g-1). The second child's mean is b0=1-4u delta. All its nonempty coefficients have zero matching coefficient in the constant child. Hence q0=(1+b0^2)/2 and m0=(1-|b0|)^2/4, while m_T=q_T/2 off the empty packet. Parseval gives

    mu=(1-|b0|)/2, m0=mu^2,
    J_s=mu-mu^2+mu^2 log2(q0/mu^2).

For s>=2, b0>=0 even at delta=1; thus mu_s=2u delta. For s=1, mu_1=min(delta,1-delta). The latter is essential: signed disagreement would be delta and is generally NOT the magnitude mismatch. At delta=0 or 1, expressions with zero masses are interpreted continuously.

The node has physical reach w_s=p/u. Its queried influence is d_s=2u delta, including s=1. Thus sum_s w_s d_s=2rp delta=Q and sum_s w_s mu_s<=Q. Physical data influence is p I(g), so I(F)=Q+pI(g) exactly. Every payment below is drawn from Q; pI(g) is reserved for the terminal.

### 2. Pay the complete logarithmic bill

Since q0<=1, for s>=2,

    J_s <= 2u delta+8u^2 delta^2 log2(1/(2u delta)).

For delta>0 write L=log2(1/(2delta)). Each summand 2^-s(s+L) is nonnegative for s>=2 and delta<=1. Therefore its finite sum is bounded by the infinite sum, even when L<0. Using sum_(s>=2)2^-s=1/2 and sum_(s>=2)s2^-s=3/2 gives

    sum_(s=2..r) w_s J_s
    <=2p delta[(r-1)+6delta+2delta L]
    <=2p delta(r+3).

The scalar inequality 6delta+2delta log2(1/(2delta))<=4 on [0,1] follows because its derivative is 6+2L-2c>=4-2c>0 and its value at 1 is 4. Here c<2 follows from ln2>1/2. The delta=0 limit is zero.

At the last node, set a=min(delta,1-delta)<=delta. The preceding packet formula and the scalar maximum x log2(1/x)<=c/e yield

    J_1 <= a+2a^2 log2(1/a) <= (1+2c/e)delta.

If r>=2, w_1=2p and these estimates give

    J_tree <=2p delta[r+4+2c/e]
           <=(3+c/e) Q.

The last inequality uses r>=2. If r=1, J_tree<= (1+2c/e)Q <=(3+c/e)Q, because c/e<2. Adding the full linear allowance 3c sum w_s mu_s<=3c Q proves kappa=3+c(3+1/e).

The strict bound kappa<8 is rationally certified: e>8/3 and ln2>=56/81 imply (3+1/e)/ln2 < (27/8)(81/56)=2187/448<5. Thus kappa<3+5=8. No floating approximation supplies a sign in this argument.

### 3. Exact entropy and terminal ledger

Independently, with eta(t)=t log2(1/t), m=1-2delta and v=4delta(1-delta), the spectrum gives

    H(F)-pH(g)
    =eta((1-2pdelta)^2)-p eta(m^2)
     +4p(1-p)delta^2 log2(1/(4p^2delta^2))+2rpv.

This expression includes the exceptional empty-control/data coefficient and ALL terminal entropy. The exact path costs telescope to this value; the upper mismatch bill bounds it by kappa Q. For terminal allowance K I(g),

    E sum(J+3c mu)+p K I(g)
    <=kappa Q+K pI(g)<=max(kappa,K) I(F).

Inactive leaves are constants with zero influence and entropy. Nothing assumes an FEI bound on arbitrary g: the terminal K is an explicit hypothesis.

### 4. Arbitrary depth without spending influence twice

Given a syntactic expression with fresh activation controls and physically disjoint product factors, construct its tree recursively. At an activation expose controls, stop on failure, and on success execute the core tree. At a product execute each factor's tree in any fixed order. If a residual factor is constant, its sign only changes the residual product's global output sign. For independent factors, squared spectra tensorize; H and I add, and all split q,m,J are unchanged by multiplication by an unqueried disjoint Boolean factor, since its Fourier squared masses sum to one. Thus factorwise path bills add as well. Global output negation leaves these quantities unchanged.

By induction over the expression, every activation pays its newly queried controls and passes its reserved weighted core influence to the core tree. Each product sums physically disjoint budgets. The expression tree is finite and each queried physical coordinate is used at most once along a path. At the stopping leaves, the remaining function is a product of the named certified terminals on disjoint cubes, with the sum of their valid FEI allowances. The constant is the maximum of kappa and their constants, independent of activation depth, arity, bias and number of factors.

For regular terminals take C_reg=log2(4+e)+2log2(e*pi)>8; for bounded-overlap terminals use 41+7log2(k0)+(29/5)log2(M0)>8; for uniform threshold/parity formula terminals use 744. The control closure preserves each of these constants. These are source-reported terminal theorems used conditionally on their recovered acceptance; this run does not re-audit their full proofs. The affine-dimension-four terminal theorem reviewed here has constant 7/2+2/ln2<8, so its activation closure has constant kappa<8.

First unsupported universal line: every arbitrary Boolean root admits such a finite fresh-activation/disjoint-product decomposition into certified terminals, or a different cheap physical tree reaching such terminals. No such representation theorem is proved. Arbitrary cores admitted as leaves would leave pH(g) unpaid and preserve full-FEI hardness via tensor amplification. Shared-input products and general signed multiplexer cells are excluded by actual hypothesis failures, not assumed to satisfy this lemma.

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

For every finite uniform physical control cube y and DISJOINT finite uniform core cube x, let c(y) be any Boolean indicator, a(y)=1-2c(y) its sign encoding, and u(x) any Boolean sign. Define

    p=Pr(a=-1), delta=Pr(u=-1), V_a=4p(1-p), V_u=4delta(1-delta),
    F(x,y)=1+c(y)(u(x)-1).

All entropy is in bits; Fourier coefficients are normalized Walsh coefficients. H_+(f) is the unnormalized NONEMPTY contribution sum_(S nonempty) fhat(S)^2 log2(1/fhat(S)^2), not entropy conditioned on nonemptiness. I(a) denotes sign-function total influence; if influence of the 0/1 indicator is instead defined as sum E[(D_i c)^2], it is I(a)/4. This conversion is essential.

The control-first tree exposes physical y coordinates until c is determined, or simply exposes all y coordinates. Its actual weighted leaves are u with probability p and constant +1 otherwise, with irrelevant leftover controls harmless. Let Pi_H=H(F)-pH(u) be the FULL entropy path cost and Q=Pi_I=delta I(a) the queried influence. Reserved terminal influence is pI(u). We prove

    Pi_H <= delta H_+(a)+C0 delta V_a,
    C0=2+2log2(e)+log2(e)/sqrt(e)<6.

This holds for all p,delta, dimensions and actual spectra, including deterministic signs. If H_+(a)<=T[I(a)-V_a], then Pi_H<=max(T,C0)Q. If only H(a)<=K I(a) is known, Pi_H<=(K+C0)Q. Adding a terminal allowance L I(u) gives complete root constants max(T,C0,L), respectively max(K+C0,L). The terminal may itself use a paid finite stopping tree; its reserved influence is multiplied by p exactly once.

Arbitrary repeated variable occurrences INSIDE the representation of c are permitted: c is treated as one actual Boolean function, not a syntactic sum of gate charges. Sharing physical variables BETWEEN c and u, or between separate control modules, is not covered. That sharing changes the actual terminal partition and invalidates pH(u).

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### 1. Exact arbitrary-controller spectrum

Write eta(t)=t log2(1/t), eta(0)=0, and phi(t)=eta((1-2t)^2). For a nonempty core set S and any control set T,

    Fhat(S,T)=uhat(S) chat(T),
    chat(empty)=p, chat(T)=-ahat(T)/2 for T nonempty.

For empty S and nonempty T, Fhat(empty,T)=delta ahat(T). The global empty coefficient is 1-2pdelta. Parseval for the indicator gives sum chat(T)^2=p, and its raw spectral entropy is

    sum_T eta(chat(T)^2)=eta(p^2)+H_+(a)/4+V_a/2.

Summing the entropy of all NONEMPTY core rows and the empty-core/nonempty-control row yields the exact identity

    H_+(F)=delta H_+(a)+pH_+(u)+G(p,delta),
    G=V_u eta(p^2)+V_u V_a/2+delta^2 V_a log2(1/delta^2).

The last term is zero at delta=0 and 1 by continuity. Thus

    Pi_H=delta H_+(a)+G+phi(pdelta)-p phi(delta).

This keeps both exceptional empty coefficients, rather than deleting the negative terminal subtraction. At p=1 it cancels to Pi_H=0; at delta=1 it gives Pi_H=H(a). These endpoint checks are also exact finite certificate checks.

Physical edge counting gives I_x(F)=pI(u), I_y(F)=delta I(a), I(F)=pI(u)+delta I(a). These are dedicated disjoint budgets. The weighted sum of actual queried control influences is Q for every control-only tree determining c; its remaining entropy is exactly pH(u). This uses the already established physical-tree telescope, not a new telescope claim.

### 2. A global bias correction without an endpoint logarithmic loss

Set b=log2(e). The function phi is C^1 on [0,1]. Away from t=1/2,

    phi''(t)=-16log2|1-2t|-24b >= -24b.

The positive logarithmic singularity at 1/2 is locally integrable and phi' is continuous there. Therefore phi(t)+12bt^2 is convex on the whole interval. Apply the convex chord between 0 and delta at pdelta, with phi(0)=0, to get

    phi(pdelta)-p phi(delta)<=12b p(1-p)delta^2=3b delta^2 V_a.

Also -ln p<=(1-p)/p gives eta(p^2)<=b V_a/2, including p=0,1 by continuity. For delta>0, divide the remaining G bound by delta V_a when V_a>0. The result is

    [G+phi(pdelta)-p phi(delta)]/(delta V_a)
    <=2b(1-delta)+2(1-delta)+3bdelta+2delta log2(1/delta)
    =2+2b+delta[b-2+2log2(1/delta)].

The scalar final term has maximum b/sqrt(e), attained at delta=1/(2sqrt(e)): differentiation gives 2log2(1/delta)-b-2=0. The continuous delta=0 limit is zero. This proves the advertised C0. The cases delta V_a=0 are obtained directly from the exact identity, so no illegal division occurs.

The inequality C0<6 is an exact elementary certificate: ln2>=56/81 and e>8/3>(8/5)^2 imply b<=81/56 and 1/sqrt(e)<5/8. Consequently C0<2+(81/56)(21/8)=2597/448<6. These inequalities are rational; no floating sign is used.

Since V_a<=I(a), H_+(a)<=T[I(a)-V_a] gives

    Pi_H<=delta T[I(a)-V_a]+C0delta V_a<=max(T,C0)Q.

Ordinary H(a)<=K I(a), together with H_+(a)<=H(a), gives (K+C0)Q. The actual terminal H(u)<=L I(u) costs pL I(u). Therefore the complete expected path PLUS terminal bound is the stated maximum against Q+pI(u)=I(F), with no reused ancestral influence.

### 3. What this does and does not say about mismatch upper bills

Pi_H is the full ACTUAL entropy decrement, the leaf-partition quantity required by B06 R2. It is not equal to the particular retained magnitude-mismatch upper bill from stage 1. At every physical query the retained KL/log charge J_v satisfies J_v<=Delta_v H. Thus sum w_v J_v<=Pi_H; adding its upper allowance 3b sum w_v mu_v costs at most an additional 3bQ. If a consumer insists on that upper bill, a valid controller-strong rate is max(T,C0)+3b, not silently max(T,C0). The stage-1 point-control bound on that particular upper bill remains unchanged.

### 4. Strong composition and arbitrary finite nesting

Let D=4pdelta(1-p)(1-delta). The physical deficit has the exact nonreuse decomposition

    I(F)-Var(F)=delta[I(a)-V_a]+p[I(u)-V_u]+D.

When D>0, the previously computed correction obeys

    G/D=2+2p log2(1/p)/(1-p)+2delta log2(1/delta)/(1-delta)
        <=alpha, alpha=2+4b<8.

The boundary cases have G=D=0 where required and follow by continuity. Thus strengthened controller/core certificates T_a,T_u compose with constant max(T_a,T_u,alpha). This is the standard disjoint FEI+ composition mechanism specialized to a negative-event conjunction, now stated with an explicit scalar gate correction and the physical stopping budgets. The scalar alpha is sharp for G/D: take actual Boolean a and u equal -1 except at one point on separate r-bit cubes, so p=delta=1-2^-r and the ratio tends to 2+4b. This is sharpness of a correction functional, not an optimal FEI constant or a disproof family.

For a strengthened constant at least b, H_+(f)<=T[I(f)-Var(f)] also implies H(f)<=TI(f), since eta((Ef)^2)<=b Var(f). Therefore finite disjoint conjunction/De Morgan expression trees inherit the indicated complete terminal-inclusive constant, with no dependence on depth. There is no claim for shared physical support.

More directly, if EACH control module has an ordinary certificate K0 and an innermost core has terminal allowance L, sequential fresh activation trees have complete constant max(K0+C0,L), independent of the number of modules. At each new activation the queried module uses Q and passes p times the existing core tree's full budget forward. Intermediate cores need not remain regular. For regular or character-regular controller and terminal modules use K0=L=C_reg, giving C_reg+C0<14.74. This is a concrete conditional application of recovered controller certificates, not a new claim that arbitrary control indicators are regular.

### 5. Point-control strengthening and a certified obstruction

For the point sign a=1-2A_r, p=2^-r, I(a)=2rp, Var(a)=4p(1-p), H_+(a)=8p(1-p)(r-1). For r=1 both H_+ and I-Var vanish. For r>=2 the bound H_+(a)<=6[I(a)-Var(a)] reduces to

    2r-8+4p(r+2)>=0.

At r=2 it is equality, at r=3 it is positive, and for r>=4 it is immediate. Consequently the arbitrary-controller theorem proves Pi_H<=6Q for EVERY unbalanced point-activated core. This improves the ACTUAL leaf-partition rate while retaining the different stage-1 mismatch-bill result.

A tax-free controller charge and correction coefficient four both fail on an ACTUAL three-bit function: take a dictator controller (p=1/2, H_+(a)=H(a)=0, V_a=I(a)=1) and core u=D_2 (delta=1/4). The root is D_3 and terminals are D_2 or +1. Direct integer spectra give

    Pi_H=3-(9/8)log2(3), Q=1/4,
    Pi_H/Q=12-(9/2)log2(3)>4.

The strict sign is the integer certificate 3^9=19683<65536=2^16. It follows that the best universal additive coefficient in Pi_H<=delta H_+(a)+Cdelta V_a is at least this exact ratio, whereas the proof gives C<=C0<6. No optimal coefficient claim is made. The finite witness does not refute FEI.

### 6. Honest universal frontier

Setting u identically -1 gives F=a, Pi_H=H(a), Q=I(a). Hence a fixed finite K paying control-first Pi_H for EVERY controller implies full FEI with the SAME K. Conversely full FEI C and the proved bias bound give a universal control-first rate C+C0. Thus this arbitrary-controller endpoint is FEI-equivalent in finiteness and cannot be declared solved by merely transferring its unpaid H_+(a).

The first unsupported line toward full FEI is a universal controller certificate, or a new structurally justified decomposition/ownership law for overlapping controllers that pays their full controller entropy and terminal cores. Allowing c and u to share inputs invalidates the exact leaf cost pH(u); no overlap extension is asserted. Further fresh nesting on one unchanged core merely combines control indicators and is not a new universal mechanism.

# A029 / B06: actual child-deficit transport and depth-two gain

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

All functions are actual Boolean signs on the uniform cube; H uses bits,
I is total ordinary physical influence, and D_K=KI-H. Full FEI remains OPEN.
The B06 lead's v1 direction replaces rederivation of its R2 telescope with
a bounded measurement of nonlocal gain. For nonconstant f define

  r1(f)=min_{i:Inf_i>0} [H(f)-average H(f_i)]/Inf_i(f),
  r2(f)=min_{T:1<=depth(T)<=2,Pi_I>0} Pi_H(T)/Pi_I(T).

The root must query a relevant coordinate. Each actual physical child may
stop or query a remaining relevant coordinate, independently. The second
query may differ by branch. Root-only trees are included. Pi_H is root
entropy minus weighted terminal entropy; Pi_I is root influence minus
weighted terminal influence. Constants have no divided ratio.

**Certified finite result:** for every nonconstant f in dimensions 1..4,
0<=r1-r2<=2. The maximum is exactly 2. Equality holds precisely for
(a) functions with two essential variables that are signed input/output
variants of AND2, and (b) four-variable bent functions. Here bent means
all 16 squared Fourier coefficients are 1/16. There are 976 equality
truth tables across the enumerated dimensions: 8, 24, 48 AND2 extensions
in dimensions 2,3,4 respectively, and 896 essential four-variable bent
functions. This finite result is not extrapolated to arbitrary n.

**Analytic scoped result:** for the original B05 sparse activated bent
point-surgery family with even k>=4, r=2k, delta=2^-k, p=2^-r,
both physical selector children satisfy D_4>=p(k-3), and the selector
parent satisfies

  D_4(f)>=p[k-3-delta(3k+1/2)]>0.

This explicitly pays an unbounded local-selector ratio from proved child
slack at K=4. No universal induction hypothesis is used for these children.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### What the largest gap means analytically

Take g to be a signed AND of two variables. Its four squared Fourier
coefficients are 1/4, so H(g)=2 and I(g)=1; both influences are 1/2.
Each coordinate restriction is one constant and one signed dictator,
both of entropy zero. Thus Delta_i H=2 and r1=4. Query one coordinate,
then query the dictator child and stop the constant child. Pi_H=2 and
Pi_I=1, so r2=2. No proper tree on these two variables can consume more
than all influence or erase more than all entropy; the root-only ratio
is 4 and the complete tree ratio is 2.

At K=2, the root debt Delta_i H-K Inf_i equals 1. Actual child deficits
are 0 and 2, so the weighted reserve is exactly 1. Revealing the dictator
uses its influence but produces zero entropy drop, creating credit 2
at child reach probability 1/2. All terminal deficits are zero. The
credit is spent once at the parent; it is not also retained at a leaf.

A genuinely four-essential-variable equality witness is truth mask 854
in the stated least-significant-coordinate convention. Root coordinate
0 has child masks 30 and 17. Up to signs they are zg and g on the
remaining variables, with H=2 in both branches and I=2 and 1. The root
has flat spectrum, H=4, I=2, Delta_0 H=2 and Inf_0=1/2. Query the
independent character z in the zg child and stop the other child:
Pi_H=2, Pi_I=1. The terminal entropy is still 2! At K=2 the children
have deficits 2 and 0, paying root debt 1 exactly. This exhibits the
entropy-preserving child query that makes nonlocal payment possible.

Every essential n=4 equality table is a quadratic Boolean sign with a
nonsingular alternating 4x4 adjacency matrix. The classification script
checks this directly by Boolean Mobius transform and direct Walsh sums,
and reconstructs the complete set from 28 nonsingular graphs times 32
affine signs. The four graph degree multisets are matching (1,1,1,1),
path (1,1,2,2), triangle with attached leaf (1,2,2,3), and complete
graph (3,3,3,3). For any quadratic, squaring the Walsh transform shows
that its Fourier support is an affine translate of the image of its
adjacency matrix, with equal masses; hence entropy equals matrix rank.
For completeness: the autocorrelation at shift t is zero unless At=0,
and otherwise is a sign character on ker(A). Fourier inversion of that
character gives the stated affine flat support of size 2^rank(A).

In the first three graph types, query the neighbor of a leaf vertex.
Both three-variable children have rank 2, hence H=2; the leaf coordinate
is isolated and its derivative is constant, with influence 1 in one
child and 0 in the other. Query it only in the influence-1 child.
The resulting entropy cost is 2 and influence cost is 1. For the
complete graph, each child is a rank-2 triangle; query any child
coordinate in both branches. Each two-variable leaf retains a quadratic
edge and H=2, while queried child influence is 1/2. Again the costs
are 2 and 1. Every root has local ratio 4.

These trees are optimal analytically too. After any root query, a
rank-2 three-variable child graph is either one edge plus an isolated
vertex, a two-edge path, or a triangle. A second query that drops
entropy has (Delta H,Inf)=(2,1/2). Queries preserving entropy have
influence 1/2, except an isolated vertex which has influence 0 or 1.
For that isolated case the two sibling influences are complementary,
so the weighted influence Z of all entropy-preserving second queries
is at most 1/2. Let E be weighted influence of the entropy-dropping
second queries. Then

  Pi_H=2+4E, Pi_I=1/2+Z+E<=1+E,
  Pi_H/Pi_I>=(2+4E)/(1+E)>=2.

Thus the gain 2 for all 896 bent functions is explained without relying
only on numerical pattern recognition. The finite census excludes every
other equality class and every larger gap.

### Actual-child transport on B05

The complete proof is saved immediately in B05_TRANSPORT.md. Here are
the steps needed to audit the budget. For F=1+A(u-1), mu=Eu in [0,1],
c=1-mu, its constant coefficient is 1-pc; nonempty-control/empty-data
coefficients have magnitude pc; each nonempty-data coefficient p uhat(T)
is repeated 2^r times. With h(t)=-t log2 t, the exact entropy is

  H(F)=p[H(u)-h(mu^2)]+2rp[(1-mu^2)+(1-p)c^2]
       +p(1-p)h(c^2)+h((1-pc)^2).

Using h(t)<=(1-t)/ln2, (1-mu^2)+c^2=2c and the actual activation
influence I(F)=p[I(u)+rc] gives

  H(F)<=pH(u)+4rpc+2p/ln2,
  D_4(F)>=p[4I(u)-H(u)-2/ln2].

For the actual b,b' cores, Eu=sqrt(delta) or sqrt(delta)-2delta,
I(u)=k/2 or k/2+2k delta. Both means lie in [0,1]. The elementary
dimensional entropy bound H(u)<=k gives D_4(G),D_4(H)>=p(k-3), using
ln2>2/3. These are proved child facts, not assumptions of full FEI.

Selector influence is d=p delta=2^-3k. By the baseline split identity,
conditioning and the scalar JS bound,

  Delta_y H<=h2(d)+(2/ln2)d<=d(3k+3/ln2),
  Delta_y H-4d<=p delta(3k+1/2).

Since 2^-k(3k+1/2) decreases for k>=4 and equals 25/32 at k=4,
the averaged child reserve is larger than the selector debt. B06 R2
then gives the stated strictly positive lower bound on D_4(f).
This succeeds on the original all-coordinate obstruction while keeping
the whole child entropy in the ledger. It does not pay arbitrary cores.

### Nonreuse and the exact remaining universal gap

Use B06 R2 as the accounting interface, with b_v=K Inf_{i_v}-Delta_{i_v}H.
For every physical cut L, D_K(root)=sum_{rho in L} w_rho D_K(f_rho)
plus the b_v terms strictly above the cut. Expanding a child replaces
its deficit by its descendant cut deficits and increments; it never adds
them to the unexpanded deficit. Finite induction on successive cuts
gives an ownership rule for all transfers: each terminal deficit and
each signed increment has exactly one owner, identified by physical
node and reach probability. Internal reserves may be used as shorthand
only until expanded. Negative terminal deficits must remain signed.

The repeated-slack mistake has an actual Boolean witness: for m-bit
parity, D_K=Km, but summing weighted actual deficits of every internal
node in a complete tree gives K*m*(m+1)/2. All that apparent extra
reserve consists of the same still-unqueried coordinates repeated at
successive cuts. There is no entropy debt in this example, so any such
reserve-summing rule is already invalid on a trivial FEI case.

Disjoint tensors of m signed AND2 factors retain r1=4 and r2=2. A tree
that clears one factor consumes influence 1 and entropy 2, leaving the
other factors intact. More sharply, for F=g_AND2*h on disjoint variables,
the same tree has Pi_H=2, Pi_I=1 and terminal functions equal to signed
h. Thus D_K(F)=D_K(h)+(K-2). The cheap depth-two step does not erase or
prove the seed's entropy bound. A universal proof still needs a physical
tree whose total paid increments plus actual terminal deficits establish
D_K>=0 for every seed, at one dimension-independent K. This is the
first unsupported universal line. No new broad universal candidate is
opened while B06's pending-review queue is capped.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

Write f=sum_S a_S chi_S. Fix A to rho. The restricted coefficient at T is sum_{S\A=T} a_S chi_{S cap A}(rho). If the projection is injective on occupied support, this sum has one nonzero term; hence the full positive squared-mass multiset is unchanged, H(f_rho)=H(f), and I(f_rho)=sum_S |S\A|a_S^2=I(f)-sum_{i in A}Inf_i(f). Spectral A-membership is determined by the complement, and all physical assignments have the same labelled complement spectrum: both block erasure and channel information vanish. If support distance is >=L, projection collisions require >=L deleted coordinates. Thus every adaptive tree of depth <=L-1 has zero entropy decrement on every branch. No rare-branch qualification is needed.

Construct F_L=g(y), y_i=product_j x_ij, L>=2. The seed label S maps to the union of its L-coordinate blocks. This injective map multiplies sizes and distances by L, so H(F_L)=H(g), Inf_ij(F_L)=Inf_i(g), I(F_L)=L I(g). While each block retains ell_i>=1 coordinates, the residual has H(g) and I=sum_i ell_i Inf_i(g), independently of assignments. Querying L-1 coordinates per block yields a genuine fair tree of depth n(L-1), with 2^[n(L-1)] equally probable coordinate-sign translates of g as leaves. Hence E H_leaf=H(g), E I_leaf=I(g), Pi_H=0, Pi_I=(L-1)I(g), and leaf/root H/I amplification exactly L when H(g)>0. L=2^k gives iterated pair-expansion amplification 2^k, but undoing it requires n(2^k-1) physical queries, not k singleton queries.

For nonconstant g and L>=d+2, every restriction of <=d coordinates retains at least two inputs in every block. In a relevant block, fix other block parity values witnessing a nonzero seed derivative. The derivative in one physical coordinate equals the product of its companion block inputs times that nonzero seed derivative. Flipping a second input reverses the sign. Thus the residual is nonunate, even after arbitrary coordinate sign reversals. No depth-d physical tree can have only C001-regular leaves. For amplification at one singleton step take g_r=1-2 indicator_{all+} and G_r,m=g_r product_j z_j. ## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

Use Q_C(v)=[D_v-Cd_v+E Q_C(child)]_+, zero at constant leaves. Its least-nonnegative property is backward induction. The optimal stopping representation follows by choosing stop for zero or query and continue; it implies [H-CI]_+<=Q_C<=H. These baseline assertions are reconstructed in REVIEW.md; no new entropy/influence telescope is claimed.

Let q=Q_C(g,T). In an injective compression of F_L=g(product_j x_ij), D=0 at every prefix, each query in block i has d=Inf_i(g), and each compressed core has the same translated continuation reserve q. With ell_i surviving inputs/block and b_v=sum_i(ell_i-1)Inf_i(g), the exact solution is Q_C(v)=[q-Cb_v]_+. The algebra [-Cd+[q-C(b-d)]_+]_+=[q-Cb]_+ holds for C,d>=0. This proves the formula for every adaptive compression order that completes the same partition. The root value is [q-C(L-1)I(g)]_+; m parity spectators give [q-Cm]_+. A zero reserve at the root can therefore precede positive reserve on every branch without any entropy drop.

The alternative whole-block simulation queries L physical inputs whenever T queries a seed bit. Its first L-1 queries have zero entropy decrement; the last has exactly the seed decrement D. Every query in that block has influence d, and the parity outcomes are fair. Combining the nested positive parts yields [D-LCd+E Q_child]_+. Hence Q_C(F_L,block-simulation T)=Q_(LC)(g,T). Increasing a stopped-prefix price from C to LC loses at most C(L-1)I(g), because the prefix's spent influence is at most I(g). Thus [Q_C(g,T)-C(L-1)I(g)]_+<=Q_(LC)(g,T). This comparison is conditional on the specified core tree and does not characterize all policies.

For ordinary addressing A_a, H=2a,I=1+a/2. In data-first T, stopping after all data reveals spends influence1 and leaves a random sign table on a address bits of entropy<=a. Therefore Q_C(A_a,T)>=[a-C]_+. Set C=4,L=2. Compression-first has Q_root=[q-4I(A_a)]_+=0 because q<=2a<2a+4. Whole-block data-first has Q_root=Q_8(A_a,T)>=[a-8]_+. In the latter data-block prefix the actual queried influence is2 and retained expected influence is a; retained entropy is<=a. Both completed trees have Pi_H=2a,Pi_I=a+2. Extending constant leaves with all remaining zero-influence queries makes their physical leaf partition exactly the same set of singleton inputs without changing Q. Their reserve difference therefore grows at least a-8 even with the same completed partition and same telescoped total debt -2a-8. The root H/I=2a/(a+2)<2 throughout. This is an order-sensitive stopped-prefix reserve obstruction, not an FEI counterexample.

For the concrete small A_3 data-first core, the exact recursion gives q=(9/32)log2(3)-3/8. Integer inequalities3^9>2^14 and3^3<2^5 certify1/16<q<3/32. At C=4, z A_3 with spectator-first continuation has Q_root=0 and reserve q on both children. Their H/I are already below4; a positive Q is a constraint on future prefixes rather than a child FEI deficit. For the all-a spectator variant m=ceil(2a/C), C>0, q<=2a implies root Q=0 while q>=[a-C]_+ reappears on every compressed-core branch. Unpaid prefix costs excluding the spectators must not be substituted for the complete root debt, which includes their prepaid influence.

For a general zero-entropy subtree with nonnegative leaf reserves q_l and nonnegative cumulative path cost b_l, [E q_l-C E b_l]_+<=Q_root<=E[q_l-Cb_l]_+. Full continuation or immediate stopping proves the lower bound. Any strategy aborted before a leaf has payoff minus a nonnegative spent cost; complete continuation on a path has payoff q_l-Cb_l. Thus the pathwise positive part bounds every adapted strategy, proving the upper bound. It is an oracle bound and may be strict. An actual example: for a>=13, z A_a at C=4, use data-first on one spectator branch (q>=9) and address-first on the other (reserve0, since each address reveal has D=2,d=1/2). The parent reserve is q/2-4, whereas the oracle upper bound is q/2-2: gap exactly2. These child spectra agree, but their prescribed continuations differ. No claim that Q is a function of the Boolean function alone is made.

A064's terminal-corrected bill P=H(node)-E H(final leaf) is instead invariant through exact compression with translated continuations. Stop at g and P=0, with all H(g) retained at the terminal; continue to constants and P=H(g) throughout the plateau. Its resource bound and the priced minimal Q_C are distinct. The complete proofs and construction details are in RESERVE_TRANSPORT.md.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line
The complete proof is CONDITIONAL_PHASE_THEOREM.tex. On an affine physical cell a+V, the signed square-Walsh identity averages the quadratic polar character over v; it vanishes unless the difference w lies in the polar kernel. The remaining signed sum on that kernel is either its full size or zero. Hence the normalized row spectrum is uniform on an affine coset of dimension k+r. Its entropy is k+r, while every varying coordinate costs half a unit of expected spectral degree and there are at least k+r varying coordinates. Distinct X labels retain each row without coherent collision. The chain rule keeps the whole conditional entropy, rather than charging a marginal twice. Empty labels and zero influence are covered.

Restriction stability is exact for all Y coordinate restrictions, and for X restrictions that keep projected labels distinct. A fresh-Y tensor factor must be a quadratic phase by fixing one occupied physical row point. Conversely, full physical restriction closure of ordinary addressing recovers any Boolean truth table by setting the data bits to that table. Thus demanding all X restrictions creates an FEI-strength endpoint. The first unsupported universal inference is an influence payment after X labels collide or after nonquadratic row phases are admitted. No assertion of universal stability or unrestricted conditional payment is made.

The normalized non-Boolean control psi_N=N^(-1/2)sum_i y_i has conditional entropy log2 N but I_Y=1, violating the constant-two inequality for N>=5. Thus the statement cannot be inferred from normalization and marginal degree alone. The class excludes cubic tensor phases by their unique degree-three binary monomial. It allows quadratic tensor factors, whose entropy is explicitly paid.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

The complete short derivations are in CANCELLATION_FAILURE.tex. For even n the quadratic bent sign has flat squared spectrum, so H=Hinf=n and I=n/2. Every nonzero signed XOR autocorrelation is zero by f^2=1, but its absolute counterpart is one. Thus total unsigned autocorrelation divided by I is 2(2^n-1)/n and diverges. Triangle inequality is valid in the direction |sum terms|<=sum absolute terms; inferring an upper bound for the right-hand side from the vanishing left-hand side reverses the implication. This refutes the unsigned payment, not an unspecified signed weighted target.

For the tribes sign h_{w,m}, let q=2^-w and r=1-q. Its constant amplitude is 1-2r^m. A Fourier set meeting exactly j tribes has squared amplitude 4q^(2j)r^(2(m-j)) and multiplicity binom(m,j)(2^w-1)^j. Its influence is 2wmq r^(m-1). These follow by expanding the product of independent failures and counting pivotal edges. The six-bit h_{2,3} has histogram {25/1024:1,81/1024:9,9/1024:27,1/1024:27}, I=27/16, and Hinf=10-4log2(3)>2I. The last sign is exactly certified by 3^32<2^53. The twelve-bit h_{3,4} gives the stronger necessary K_min >= (512/1029)(22-2log2(353)) >2.524150672274.

The min-gap helper is itself full-FEI strength. Given ANY Boolean h, set g=y product(j=1..t)h(x_j), which is balanced, and F=(1+z)/2+(1-z)g/2. The constant and z amplitudes are 1/2, and each nonzero g amplitude supplies two amplitudes of magnitude |ghat|/2. Hence H(F)=2+tH(h)/2, Hinf(F)=2, and I(F)=1+tI(h)/2. A universal gap bound with constant K gives tH(h)<=K(tI(h)+2); letting t grow gives FEI with the SAME K. Conversely FEI bounds the gap since Hinf>=0. Thus the optimal universal constants coincide. This is an application of the paper's exact activation identity, with its extra min-entropy accounting; it is not an easier new universal payment.

Taking h=h_{2,8} gives I(h)=2187/2048 and certified 4.623452413789<H(h)<4.623452413790. For bent-core point surgery, let the bent core have even k, pad to n>=k, and flip the value at a point of core weight r. # A036 / B08: normalized collision payment on point-defect tensors

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

All logarithms are base two unless written ln. Let C be the class of all finite disjoint tensor products of f_m(x)=1-2*1_{x=x0}, m>=2, allowing arbitrary physical translations, a global output sign, character multiplication, extra character coordinates and irrelevant coordinates. All functions are genuine Boolean signs on the uniform cube. Define P(S)=fhat(S)^2, d_i=P(i in S), I=sum_i d_i, B=sum_i h_2(d_i), and the reference Q(S)=prod_i d_i^{1_{i in S}}(1-d_i)^{1_{i not in S}}. Q is fixed across sampled spectral sets. On its support define b_S=sign(fhat(S))*sqrt(Q(S)), and set b_S=0 off that support. For this class P and Q have identical support, so no sign completion is needed.

Put K=D_2(P||Q), C_b(U)=sum_S b_S b_{S xor U}, v_U=C_b(U)^2, Z=sum_U v_U, L=sum_U v_U log_2(1/v_U), R=v/Z and T=L/Z=H(R)-log_2 Z. Zero summands are zero. The following three inequalities hold on C:

1. **Named excess payment:** K >= [B-4I]_+.
2. **Normalized collision payment:** K >= T/4-8I.
3. **Separate sufficient recovery:** B <= T/4+8I.

Thus collision payment with any constant kappa on this class would imply H(f)=B-K <= (kappa+8)I; the proved kappa=8 yields 16I. Independently, the proof of (1) already gives the stronger H<=4I. The contribution is the explicit divergence/collision ledger and the recovery estimate, not a new FEI class claim or a novelty claim for the known point-defect entropy bound. Constants are conservative.

These estimates are NOT asserted for arbitrary Boolean functions, arbitrary sparse activation of a seed, physical restrictions, overlapping products, or near-tensor surgery. In particular the full-support low-I universal collision premise remains open.
